enforcement_note: An OpenAPI validator checks the schema matches the document; it cannot tell whether the method is semantically right or the resource model coherent.
condition: When designing or changing an interface other systems call.
rule: Audit HTTP semantics, contract stability and API-specific authorization, as questions.
ai_action: Work through the checklist against the code in question. Report the answers, including the ones that pass -- a checklist that only ever surfaces problems reads as noise. Where an answer is 'I cannot tell from here', say so rather than assuming the safe answer.

checklist.question: Is each method's effect consistent with whether it is defined as safe?
Are the idempotent methods actually idempotent when retried?
checklist.remediation_hint: PUT and DELETE must give the same effect on repeat.

checklist.question: Does the status code carry the outcome, rather than a 200 with an error body?
checklist.remediation_hint: Return the code that matches the semantics.

checklist.question: Is this change additive, or would it break a caller that has not redeployed?
checklist.remediation_hint: Add a field; do not repurpose or remove one.
checklist.group_condition: When the interface has existing consumers

checklist.question: Is every deployed version of this API inventoried, including the old one still running?
checklist.group_condition: When the interface has existing consumers

checklist.question: Is object-level authorization enforced for every identifier the caller supplies?
checklist.group_condition: When the endpoint returns or modifies data

checklist.question: Are properties the caller may not set filtered on input, and may not see filtered on output?
checklist.remediation_hint: Bind to an explicit allowed-field list.
checklist.group_condition: When the endpoint returns or modifies data

checklist.question: Is data received FROM another API validated as untrusted?
checklist.remediation_hint: Validate third-party responses before acting on them.
checklist.group_condition: When the endpoint returns or modifies data

anti_pattern: Do not convert these questions into prescriptions. A question makes you look at the code and survives a codebase it was not written for; a prescription tells you what to type and stops being right the moment the context differs.
